citation.statement: Plasma surrounds a levitated magnetic dipole in a magnetosphere-like geometry.
citation.section: 9.5.1 Levitated dipoles
citation.scope: Nested field surfaces surround the levitated superconducting ring; far field is dipolar. Earth's atmospheric intersections make actual magnetospheric boundaries different from closed laboratory flux surfaces.

claims.original_statement: Inward particle redistribution and improved hot-electron stability in studied discharges

citation.statement: Inward particle redistribution and improved hot-electron stability in studied discharges
citation.section: 1 Centrally Peaked Density during Levitation; 2 Scrape-of-layer and Global Energy Confinement; 3 Low frequency fluctuations
citation.scope: Supported-versus-levitated LDX discharges show profile redistribution and improved hot-electron interchange stability under stated heating/fueling conditions. Four-channel inversion has limited resolution/core uncertainty. Central peaking does not itself prove increased particle lifetime; low-fueling HEI bursts can still occur. Not universal all-plasma stability, better transport on every metric or reactor-grade confinement.

claims.original_statement: Internal-coil neutron protection, cryogenic operation and reactor-scale validation

citation.statement: Internal-coil neutron protection, cryogenic operation and reactor-scale validation
citation.section: 9.5.1 Levitated dipoles / fusion applications
citation.scope: Supports protection of the internal superconducting coil from D-T neutron irradiation. No universal blanket thickness or lifetime, and weakly neutronic proposals are not assumed neutron-free; cryogenic/scale limits have complementary report support.

claims.original_statement: Internal-coil neutron protection, cryogenic operation and reactor-scale validation

citation.statement: Internal-coil neutron protection, cryogenic operation and reactor-scale validation
citation.section: Research Accomplishments; 2 Scrape-of-layer and Global Energy Confinement; 3 Low frequency fluctuations
citation.scope: Supports cryostat cooling/re-cooling and laboratory confinement measurements. Reactor-scale validation is an explicit review requirement inferred from the laboratory scope, not a reported universal failure. Cryostat three-hour float time is distinct from >20second plasma discharges; energetic-electron temperatures are not bulk-ion fusion temperatures or net-power evidence.

citation.scope: Names FRC and distinguishes predominantly poloidal geometry from a spheromak. A small toroidal field is possible without adopting a force-free spheromak equilibrium.

claims.original_statement: A compact plasma has predominantly poloidal magnetic field with a reversed-field core.

citation.statement: A compact plasma has predominantly poloidal magnetic field with a reversed-field core.
citation.section: 9.3.2.1 Field geometry; Fig9.29 / weak toroidal field discussion
citation.scope: Typical closed poloidal surfaces contain a field-reversal O-null, with end X-nulls and open exterior field lines. Predominantly poloidal does not exclude weak toroidal fields; no perfect particle containment or global stability.

claims.original_statement: High beta and compact geometry

citation.statement: High beta and compact geometry
citation.section: 9.3 compact geometry / 9.3.2.1–3 high-beta equilibrium
citation.scope: Simply connected linear vessel and high pressure relative to confining magnetic pressure; beta is geometry/definition dependent and locally singular at a field null. Neither high beta nor compactness proves fusion gain, confinement quality or commercial simplicity.

claims.original_statement: Sustainment, particle losses and stability

citation.statement: Sustainment, particle losses and stability
citation.section: 9.3.2.2–4 losses, rotation and tilt stability
citation.scope: Diffusive separatrix losses and rotation/tilt modes matter. Fluid tilt predictions differ from resilience of particular kinetic experiments; stabilization is configuration dependent, not universally absent or achieved.

claims.original_statement: Sustainment, particle losses and stability

citation.statement: Sustainment, particle losses and stability
citation.section: 9.3.2.5 Steady state FRCs
citation.scope: Historical energetic-particle and RMF current-drive approaches have performance/stability/field-surface limitations. Two-ms field reversal is not indefinite steady operation or net power; weak-field mitigation remains bounded.

claims.original_statement: Self-organised toroidal plasma carries both poloidal and toroidal magnetic fields.

citation.statement: Self-organised toroidal plasma carries both poloidal and toroidal magnetic fields.
citation.section: 9.3.1.1–3 surfaces, formation and helicity
citation.scope: Plasma currents/relaxation form poloidal and toroidal fields and near-Taylor sustainment states. Ideal nested surfaces are conditional; bubble-burst formation has wandering/open-connected field lines and heat losses.

claims.original_statement: Simply connected confinement vessel without interlocking toroidal-field coils

citation.statement: Simply connected confinement vessel without interlocking toroidal-field coils
citation.section: 9.3 simply connected vessel / SSPX geometry / HIST transition
citation.scope: No interlocking toroidal-field coils are needed for the compact confinement topology. Does not mean no bias coils, gun electrodes, flux conserver or all central structures in every implementation; HIST rod changes the configuration to spherical tokamak.

claims.original_statement: Relaxation, formation and sustained confinement

citation.statement: Relaxation, formation and sustained confinement
citation.section: 9.3.1.2–3 formation, relaxation and helicity injection
citation.scope: Formation causes reconnection and heat loss; resistive decay requires drive. CHI-associated non-axisymmetric perturbations can damage surfaces/confinement. Favorable hot-plasma extrapolations are conditional and not experimentally realized net-power proof.

claims.original_statement: Relaxation, formation and sustained confinement

citation.statement: Relaxation, formation and sustained confinement
citation.section: 9.3.1.4–5 current amplification and transport
citation.scope: Current amplification, electrode heat loads, near-edge dissipation and confinement are reactor challenges. SSPX factor2–3 and proposed reactor requirement20–30 are separate dated quantities, not demonstrated reactor drive efficiency; simulated temperatures differed from experiment.

claims.original_statement: Sustainment, electrode loads and scaling

Not current operation, net power or the distinct ten-microsecond observation of the later perspective.
